Ben —

Thanks for taking the time on Friday. Procurement looped me in with a short questionnaire so we can translate the technical sizing into contract terms. High level asks:

- Confirm recommended GPU families for our LLM mix (GPT-3.5-like and 30% larger models).
- Example throughput targets to meet our 50rps sustained / 250rps burst requirement at p95 latency < 150ms for small prompts.
- Onboarding timeline and when committed capacity can be live (we need production by 2027-01-15).
- Any operational constraints (min commitment period, burst scheduling rules, planned maintenance windows).

Attached is our internal run-rate forecast and a short traffic profile (see throughput-by-hour tab). Can you respond with a brief form-style answer that we can attach to our procurement packet?

Appreciate it —

Hi Maya —

Thanks for the detailed ask and the traffic file. Quick summary up front: we can meet the sustained 50rps and handle 250rps bursts with a mixed pool and burst-lane reservations; p95 < 150ms is achievable with the recommended GPU mix and our prefix caching strategy.

I'll send a concise questionnaire reply and our commitment playbook by EOD tomorrow. High-level notes:
- Recommended GPUs: A mix of A800-class (cost-effective for the 70% workload) + one or two H100-class slots for the 30% heavier model traffic.
- Burst handling: reserve a dedicated burst lane equal to 30% of peak, with auto-borrow from non-critical pools during off-peak hours.
- Onboarding: 6–8 weeks typical for Dedicated (provisioning, test drive, soak). To hit 2027-01-15, we should finalize contract by mid-November.

I'll loop in Lauren and Hannah for technical validation on sizing and maintenance windows.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Team — forwarding Maya's RFI (see original below). Quick ask: can you each provide short bullets I can paste into the procurement packet by tomorrow midday? Focus on: GPU families, runrate-to-slot mapping, expected p95 at target sequence lengths, maintenance windows, and any required minimum term.

Suggested starter guidance (fill/adjust):
- GPU mix: 70% A800-class (or equivalent Ampere mainstream), 30% H100-class reserved instances for heavy-context models.
- Slot mapping: 1 A800 slot ≈ 45 sustained rps for small prompts with caching; 1 H100 slot ≈ 120 sustained rps for larger models when quantized and batched.
- Burst strategy: Dedicated burst lane (30% of peak) + automated cross-pool borrow during low-util windows (midnight–06:00 local).
- Maintenance: rolling maintenance windows 02:00–05:00 Sundays (regional), customers can request blackout windows for a 6-month period after go-live.
- Minimum term: 12 months standard; 24 months preferred for deeper discounts.

Hannah — can you confirm the slot mapping numbers quickly? Karthik — note if quantized model variants change mapping. Lauren — any commercial constraints to call out for procurement?

Thanks —
Ben

Subject: Re: Fwd: RFI: Dedicated capacity commitment & burst scheduling — need sizing/ops bullets

Ben / Team —

Quick validation and a couple of clarifications:
- Slot mapping (p95 targets assume prefix caching enabled and median prompt length ≈ 35 tokens):
  - A800-class slot: ~40–50 sustained rps for small prompts (p95 ≈ 90–120ms).
  - H100-class slot: ~100–130 sustained rps for larger models (p95 ≈ 110–150ms when quantized + batching).
- If StellarData runs primarily long-context (>1k tokens) workloads, swap ratio to 50/50 A800/H100.
- Burst behavior: recommend a 4x smoothing window for burst lane allocations to avoid oscillation during traffic spikes.
- Maintenance: add a single annual full-cluster upgrade (2–3 hours), otherwise rolling patches. We can support a blackout window for the first 3 months post-prod for an additional ops fee.
- Onboarding timeline: 6 weeks (standard) — week-by-week: 1) procurement & SOW signoff; 2) infra provisioning; 3) model onboarding + perf tuning; 4) soak; 5) final cutover; 6) hypercare. To meet 2027-01-15, contract needs sign-off by 2026-11-15.

I'll attach a small runbook and a sample throughput worksheet for accuracy.

Hannah
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: RFI: Dedicated capacity commitment & burst scheduling — answers + attachments

Maya / Team —

Thanks — please find our concise answers below (suitable for procurement). I also attached the Commitment Playbook (playbook PDF) and our throughput workbook for your packet.

1) Recommended GPU families- Primary pool: A800-class (cost-effective baseline for the majority of requests).- Heavy-context & high-throughput tier: H100-class reserved slots for 24/7 availability for the 30% heavier models.

2) Example throughput targets (assumptions: median prompt 35 tokens; prefix caching enabled; p95 targets as requested)- A800 slot: 40–50 sustained rps (p95 ≈ 90–120ms).- H100 slot: 100–130 sustained rps for heavier models (p95 ≈ 110–150ms after quantization and batching).- To cover a sustained 50rps baseline with 20% headroom + 250rps burst capacity: recommended pool = 2 A800 slots + 1 H100 slot + 1 burst-lane H100 (configurable).

3) Reservation & burst planning- Minimum term: 12 months standard; 24 months for enterprise discount tiers.- Burst lane: configurable dedicated burst pool; default sizing recommendation = 30% of observed peak.- Autoscaling: allowed within committed pool for non-guaranteed lanes; guaranteed lanes are not auto-scaled below committed capacity.

4) Operational constraints- Rolling maintenance windows (02:00–05:00 Sundays PST).- Blackout windows: available for first 3 months post-cutover for an additional ops fee.- Onboarding: 6–8 weeks; target production date 2027-01-15 requires contract sign-off by 2026-11-15.

5) Commercial notes- Early-termination: standard pro-rata with 60-day notice; discounts reversed based on used-runway.- Invoicing cadence: monthly with committed/minimum-use reconciliation quarterly.

Attachments included: redwood_commit_playbook_v1.pdf, throughput_runbook.xlsx.

Next steps:
- Confirm SOW + term preference (12 vs 24 months).-
We'll prepare a draft SOW and DocuSign link once you confirm term.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
